title: Spatio-temporal Diffusion Point Processes

problem.claim: Spatio-temporal point processes model events associated with both time and space.

gap.claim: Existing solutions separately model temporal and spatial distributions because of computational complexity, limiting their ability to characterize joint spatio-temporal interactions.

contributions.claim: A diffusion-based parameterization framework is proposed to learn complex spatio-temporal joint distributions.
The target joint distribution is decomposed into multiple Gaussian-described steps, with a spatio-temporal co-attention module for adaptive time-space interdependence modeling.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their framework is the first to remove the dependency restrictions in existing spatio-temporal point-process solutions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across epidemiology, seismology, crime, and urban mobility reportedly outperform state-of-the-art baselines.
Further analyses reportedly validate adaptive capture of spatio-temporal interactions across scenarios.
The datasets and source code are reported to be publicly available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames spatio-temporal point processes as event collections with time and space.
Computational constraints have led prior approaches to separate temporal and spatial modeling, weakening joint interaction characterization.
The proposed framework uses diffusion modeling, Gaussian decomposition steps, and spatio-temporal co-attention to learn joint distributions.
The authors characterize the framework as removing prior restrictions on spatio-temporal dependencies.
Reported experiments and analyses indicate improved performance and adaptive interaction modeling across several application domains.

unknowns: No dataset names, dataset sizes, metrics, baselines, or quantitative results are supplied.
The abstract does not specify the diffusion process, Gaussian-step formulation, or co-attention architecture.
Computational cost, limitations, and reproducibility details are not established.
